checks.name: Required Zest packages are declared
checks.command: node -e "const p=require('./package.json');const all=Object.assign({},p.dependencies,p.devDependencies,p.peerDependencies,p.optionalDependencies);const need=['jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout','jattac.libs.web.zest-file-upload','jattac.libs.web.zest-tabs','jattac.libs.web.responsive-table','jattac.libs.web.zest-textbox','jattac.libs.web.zest-sidekick-menu','jattac.libs.web.zest-button','jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu','jattac-web-poller'].filter(n=>n!==p.name);const missing=need.filter(n=>!all[n]);if(missing.length){console.error('Missing required packages: '+missing.join(', '));process.exit(1)}console.log('All required packages are declared.')"

cannotTest: A bespoke component that merely repeats a listed package's function (a custom dropdown instead of jattac.libs.web.overflow-menu, a setInterval poller instead of jattac-web-poller) cannot be recognised by a regular expression and needs review, as does any third-party UI library not named in the import check. Package presence is checked only as a declaration in package.json; jattac.libs.web.zest-sidekick-menu is exempt because this repository is that package, and node_modules installation is not inspected. Native elements spread over several lines or shown in docs/README examples are out of scope.
